items.headline: Parliament passes BNS, BNSS and BSA to replace IPC, CrPC and Evidence Act
items.text: Parliament completed passage of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and Bharatiya Sakshya Bills, 2023, with Rajya Sabha approving them on 21 December 2023 after Lok Sabha did so on 20 December. The laws add offences such as terrorism and organised crime, drop sedition in its old form and treat electronic records as primary evidence. They received Presidential assent on 25 December 2023.
items.why: The biggest overhaul of India's criminal law since the colonial-era codes.

items.headline: Parliament passes Telecommunications Bill, 2023 repealing the Telegraph Act, 1885
items.text: Rajya Sabha passed the Telecommunications Bill, 2023 on 21 December 2023, a day after Lok Sabha, just three days after it was introduced. It repeals the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885 and the Wireless Telegraphy Act, 1933, provides for assigning spectrum, and keeps the government's powers to intercept communications and take over telecom services on specified grounds.

items.headline: Parliament passes Bill on appointment of Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners
items.text: Parliament passed the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Bill, 2023. Appointments will be made on the recommendation of a selection committee of the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM, with no role for the Chief Justice of India.

items.headline: Press and Registration of Periodicals Bill passed, replacing the 1867 Act
items.text: Lok Sabha passed the Press and Registration of Periodicals Bill, 2023 on 21 December 2023 (Rajya Sabha had passed it in August). It replaces the Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867 with online registration before a Press Registrar General, bars persons convicted of terrorism or unlawful activities from publishing periodicals, and provides for suspension or cancellation of registration.

items.headline: Parliament passes Post Office Bill, 2023 replacing the 1898 Act
items.text: Lok Sabha passed the Post Office Bill, 2023 on 18 December 2023, after Rajya Sabha passed it on 4 December. The law replaces the Indian Post Office Act, 1898, ends the Centre's exclusive privilege over letter delivery, and allows postal articles to be intercepted on grounds such as security of the State and emergency; PRS noted it has no procedural safeguards on interception.

items.headline: SC in Ram Kishor Arora v. ED: written grounds of arrest may be given within 24 hours
items.text: In Ram Kishor Arora v. Directorate of Enforcement (2023 LiveLaw (SC) 1059), a bench of Justices Bela M. Trivedi and Satish Chandra Sharma held that the ED must inform the arrestee of the grounds orally at the time of arrest but may furnish them in writing within 24 hours, and that the Pankaj Bansal ruling does not apply to arrests before 3 October 2023.

items.headline: MP High Court tells SC it won't enforce 3-year practice or 70% LLB marks rule for Civil Judge Exam 2023
items.text: In Monika Yadav v. High Court of Madhya Pradesh (W.P.(C) No. 1380 of 2023), the MP High Court told the Supreme Court it would not enforce the June 2023 amendment requiring three years' practice or 70% marks in LLB for the Civil Judge (Junior Division) exam, and candidates were allowed to take the 18 December exam under the earlier eligibility norms.

items.headline: Constitution Bench in In Re: Article 370 upholds abrogation of J&K's special status
items.text: A five-judge Constitution Bench unanimously upheld the 2019 Presidential Orders abrogating Article 370, holding it was a temporary provision, and upheld the carving out of Ladakh as a Union Territory. It directed the Election Commission to hold J&K Assembly elections by 30 September 2024 and asked that statehood be restored at the earliest.
items.why: Settled the constitutional validity of one of the most consequential changes to India's federal structure.

items.headline: Parliament passes J&K Reorganisation (Amendment) and J&K Reservation (Amendment) Bills
items.text: Rajya Sabha passed the J&K Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill, 2023 on 11 December 2023 (Lok Sabha had passed it on 6 December). It raises the Assembly's seats from 83 to 90, reserves nine seats for Scheduled Tribes, and lets the Lieutenant Governor nominate Kashmiri migrants and a representative of persons displaced from PoK. A companion Bill renamed 'weak and under-privileged classes' as OBCs.

items.headline: Parliament passes Advocates (Amendment) Bill, 2023 to curb touts in courts
items.text: With Lok Sabha's approval on 4 December 2023 (Rajya Sabha had passed it in August), Parliament cleared the Advocates (Amendment) Bill, 2023. It moves the provisions on touts from the Legal Practitioners Act, 1879 into the Advocates Act, 1961, lets High Courts and district judges frame and publish lists of touts, and punishes listed touts with up to three months' imprisonment and/or a Rs 500 fine; the 1879 Act is repealed.

items.headline: CLAT 2024 held on December 3; provisional answer key out, results scheduled for December 10
items.text: After conducting CLAT 2024 on 3 December 2023, the Consortium of NLUs released the provisional answer key on 4 December with objections open till 5 December, and scheduled the final answer key for 9 December, results for 10 December and counselling registration from 12 to 22 December.

items.headline: Cabinet extends Fast Track Special Courts scheme till March 2026
items.text: The Union Cabinet approved continuation of the centrally sponsored scheme for Fast Track Special Courts, including exclusive POCSO courts, for three more years up to March 2026 with an outlay of about Rs 1,952 crore, to expedite trials of rape and POCSO cases.

items.body: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
items.headline: Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Rules, 2023 notified, replacing Forest Conservation Rules
items.text: The Environment Ministry notified the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Rules, 2023 under the amended forest conservation law, replacing the Forest Conservation Rules, 2022 and setting out procedures for approvals for diversion of forest land and compensatory afforestation.

items.headline: NALSA hosts first Regional Conference on Access to Legal Aid for the Global South
items.text: NALSA organised the 1st Regional Conference on Access to Legal Aid: Strengthening Access to Justice in the Global South in New Delhi on 27-28 November 2023, with participation from over 40 countries, addressed among others by the Vice President and the Chief Justice of India.

items.headline: Justice M. Fathima Beevi, first woman judge of the Supreme Court, passes away at 96
items.text: Justice M. Fathima Beevi, who in 1989 became the first woman to be appointed a judge of the Supreme Court of India and later served as Governor of Tamil Nadu, passed away on 23 November 2023 at the age of 96.

items.headline: SC in State of Punjab v. Principal Secretary to Governor: Governor cannot sit on Bills indefinitely
items.text: In State of Punjab v. Principal Secretary to the Governor of Punjab (W.P.(C) No. 1224 of 2023; 2023 INSC 1017), the Supreme Court held that a Governor who withholds assent must return the Bill to the Legislature for reconsideration, cannot doubt the validity of an Assembly session, and directed the Punjab Governor to decide on pending Bills. The judgment was uploaded on 23 November.
items.why: Set constitutional limits on Governors' powers under Article 200.

items.body: Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home Affairs
items.headline: Standing Committee submits reports on BNS, BNSS and Bharatiya Sakshya Bills
items.text: The Standing Committee on Home Affairs submitted its reports on the three Bills to replace the IPC, CrPC and Evidence Act, recommending changes including narrower terminology in place of 'unsound mind', clarity on handling electronic evidence and modifications to the definition of organised crime.

items.headline: Justices Satish Chandra Sharma, Augustine George Masih and Sandeep Mehta sworn in as SC judges
items.text: Three new judges took oath as judges of the Supreme Court on 9 November 2023, bringing the Court to its full sanctioned strength of 34 judges.

items.headline: SC in Ashwini Kumar Upadhyay v. Union of India directs HCs to monitor trials against MPs/MLAs
items.text: A bench led by CJI D.Y. Chandrachud in Ashwini Kumar Upadhyay v. Union of India directed the Chief Justices of High Courts to register suo motu cases to monitor the early disposal of criminal cases pending against sitting and former legislators, instead of laying down a uniform timeline.

items.headline: AIBE XVIII postponed again to December 10; registration extended to November 16
items.text: The Bar Council of India rescheduled the All India Bar Examination XVIII to 10 December 2023, its fourth postponement, citing a clash with the CLAT PG exam and the Madhya Pradesh judicial services preliminary exam, and extended online registration till 16 November.

items.headline: SC Collegium recommends three High Court Chief Justices for elevation to Supreme Court
items.text: The Supreme Court Collegium recommended the elevation of Chief Justices Satish Chandra Sharma (Delhi HC), Augustine George Masih (Rajasthan HC) and Sandeep Mehta (Gauhati HC) as Supreme Court judges, which would take the Court to its full sanctioned strength of 34.

items.body: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
items.headline: Battery Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2023 notified
items.text: The Environment Ministry notified the Battery Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2023 under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. They tighten collection and recycling obligations, including for electric vehicle batteries.

items.headline: SC in Balram Singh v. Union of India orders end to manual scavenging, raises sewer-death compensation to Rs 30 lakh
items.text: In Dr. Balram Singh v. Union of India (2023 LiveLaw (SC) 917), the Supreme Court directed the Union and States to completely eradicate manual scavenging and increased compensation for sewer deaths to Rs 30 lakh, with Rs 20 lakh for permanent disability and at least Rs 10 lakh for other disabilities.

items.headline: Justice S. Ravindra Bhat retires from the Supreme Court
items.text: Justice S. Ravindra Bhat demitted office as a Supreme Court judge on 20 October 2023. In his farewell speech he said he was satisfied that much was done but conscious that a lot remains to be done. He authored the minority opinion in the same-sex marriage case days before retiring.

items.headline: Renewable energy consumption obligations notified for 2024-30
items.text: The Ministry of Power notified minimum renewable energy consumption obligations for designated consumers under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, with targets rising over the period 2024-30.

items.headline: Supreme Court permits use of donor gametes in surrogacy despite 2023 rule change
items.text: The Supreme Court read down the Surrogacy (Regulation) Amendment Rules, 2023, which required both gametes to come from the intending couple. It allowed use of donor gametes for intending couples meeting medical criteria under the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021.
items.why: Relief for couples unable to produce their own gametes.

items.headline: Constitution Bench in Supriyo v. Union of India declines to recognise same-sex marriage
items.text: In Supriyo @ Supriya Chakraborty v. Union of India (W.P.(C) No. 1011 of 2022; 2023 INSC 920), a five-judge bench unanimously held there is no fundamental right to marry and that same-sex marriage cannot be read into the Special Marriage Act, leaving it to Parliament. By 3:2 it declined to recognise civil unions or joint adoption by queer couples; the Centre's committee on queer couples' entitlements was noted.
items.why: Landmark ruling on marriage equality; places the issue before the legislature.

items.body: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
items.headline: Green Credit Rules, 2023 notified creating market mechanism for environmental actions
items.text: The Environment Ministry notified the Green Credit Rules, 2023, setting up a market-based mechanism that awards tradeable green credits for activities such as tree plantation and waste management, with the Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education as administrator maintaining a green credit registry.

items.headline: Aircraft Rules amended to extend pilot licence validity to ten years
items.text: The Ministry of Civil Aviation notified amendments to the Aircraft Rules, 1937. Pilot licence validity was extended from five to ten years and the prohibited radius for lights around aerodromes was widened.

items.headline: Centre brings key provisions of the Mediation Act, 2023 into force
items.text: The Ministry of Law and Justice notified (S.O. 4384(E), 9 October 2023) the commencement of several provisions of the Mediation Act, 2023, including those relating to the Mediation Council of India and related amendments, marking the first step in operationalising India's statutory mediation framework.

items.headline: SC in Pankaj Bansal v. Union of India: ED must give written grounds of arrest under PMLA
items.text: In Pankaj Bansal v. Union of India (2023 INSC 866), the Supreme Court held that the Enforcement Directorate must furnish the grounds of arrest to the accused in writing at the time of arrest under Section 19 PMLA, and that mere non-cooperation with summons is not a ground to arrest. The arrests of the Bansals were set aside.
items.why: Became the leading precedent on procedural safeguards in ED arrests.

items.headline: Law Commission advises against lowering age of consent under POCSO Act
items.text: The Law Commission recommended against reducing the age of consent under the POCSO Act from 18 to 16 years. Instead, it suggested guided judicial discretion in sentencing in cases involving tacit approval of adolescents aged 16-18, subject to conditions such as a limited age gap.

items.headline: Parliament passes Women's Reservation Bill (Constitution 128th Amendment)
items.text: The Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Eighth Amendment) Bill, 2023, introduced on September 19, was passed by the Lok Sabha on September 20 and the Rajya Sabha on September 21 during the special session. It reserves one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha, State Assemblies and the Delhi Assembly, effective after the next census-based delimitation.

items.headline: Parliamentary panel reports on prison conditions and reforms
items.text: The Standing Committee on Home Affairs submitted Report No. 245 on prisons, their conditions, infrastructure and reforms. It addressed overcrowding, bail, young offenders and the welfare of women prisoners.

items.headline: Cabinet approves eCourts Project Phase III with Rs 7,210 crore outlay
items.text: The Union Cabinet approved Phase III of the eCourts Project for four years with a financial outlay of Rs 7,210 crore. It aims to create a unified technology platform for the judiciary and a paperless interface between courts, litigants and other stakeholders, including digitisation of case records.

items.headline: Rajasthan's platform-based gig workers law receives Governor's assent
items.text: The Rajasthan Platform Based Gig Workers (Registration and Welfare) Act, 2023 received the Governor's assent on September 12, 2023. It sets up a welfare board and fund, funded by a welfare fee on aggregators, and provides for registration and social security of gig workers.
items.why: First state law in India dedicated to gig workers' welfare.

items.headline: Constitution Bench: striking down of Section 6A DSPE Act has retrospective effect
items.text: In CBI v. Dr. R.R. Kishore (2023 LiveLaw (SC) 770; 2023 INSC 817), a Constitution Bench held that the 2014 Subramanian Swamy judgment striking down Section 6A of the DSPE Act applies retrospectively, so officers of Joint Secretary rank and above lose the prior-sanction protection even for pre-2014 cases.

items.headline: Draft guidelines to curb 'dark patterns' in e-commerce released
items.text: The Department of Consumer Affairs invited comments on the draft Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023. They would prohibit deceptive design practices on e-commerce platforms and digital interfaces that mislead consumers.

items.headline: Supreme Court reserves verdict on Article 370 abrogation
items.text: The Constitution Bench reserved its judgment on the petitions challenging the abrogation of Article 370, after hearing arguments that began on August 2, 2023.

items.headline: High-Level Committee constituted on simultaneous elections
items.text: The central government constituted a High-Level Committee to examine holding simultaneous elections to Lok Sabha, State Assemblies and local bodies. It is to recommend the constitutional and legislative amendments required.
items.why: Starting point of the 'One Nation, One Election' proposal.

items.headline: Children of void or voidable marriages entitled to parents' share in Hindu joint family property
items.text: In Revanasiddappa v. Mallikarjun (2023 LiveLaw (SC) 737; 2023 INSC 783), a three-judge bench held that children born of void or voidable marriages are entitled to their parents' share in Hindu joint family property, though they do not become coparceners by birth.

items.headline: Assam delimitation order takes effect, redrawing 126 Assembly seats
items.text: The delimitation order for Assam came into effect on August 16, 2023. It redrew Assam's 126 Assembly constituencies, raising seats reserved for Scheduled Castes from eight to nine and for Scheduled Tribes from 16 to 19.

items.headline: Bills to replace IPC, CrPC and Evidence Act introduced in Lok Sabha
items.text: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and Bharatiya Sakshya Bills, 2023 were introduced in the Lok Sabha to replace the IPC, CrPC and Indian Evidence Act, and referred to the Standing Committee on Home Affairs. The BNS drops sedition as such and adds offences like terrorism and organised crime.
items.why: Start of the overhaul of India's criminal law framework.

items.headline: Monsoon Session ends: 23 Bills passed, three criminal law Bills sent to committee
items.text: The Monsoon Session concluded on August 11, 2023; 25 Bills were introduced and 23 passed. Passed Bills included the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, the CGST and IGST (Amendment) Bills on online gaming and casinos, and the IIM (Amendment) Bill.
items.why: Among the busiest law-making sessions of the 17th Lok Sabha.

items.headline: Post Office Bill, 2023 introduced to replace 1898 Act
items.text: The Post Office Bill, 2023 was introduced in Rajya Sabha on August 10, 2023. It repeals the Indian Post Office Act, 1898, retains exclusive rights over issuing postage stamps, and specifies grounds on which shipments may be intercepted.
items.why: Replaces a colonial-era postal statute.

items.headline: Parliament passes Digital Personal Data Protection Bill, 2023
items.text: The Digital Personal Data Protection Bill, 2023, introduced on August 3, was passed by the Lok Sabha on August 7 and the Rajya Sabha on August 9. It sets up a consent-based regime for processing digital personal data and a Data Protection Board of India, with exemptions for government agencies.
items.why: India's first comprehensive data protection law.

items.headline: Parliament passes Mediation Bill
items.text: The Lok Sabha passed the Mediation Bill, already cleared by the Rajya Sabha on August 1, completing its passage. The law provides for pre-litigation mediation in civil and commercial disputes, a Mediation Council of India, and makes mediated settlement agreements enforceable like court judgments.

items.headline: Parliament passes GNCTD (Amendment) Bill on control of Delhi services
items.text: The Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi (Amendment) Bill, 2023, replacing the May ordinance, was passed by Parliament after the Rajya Sabha cleared it on August 7. It applies retrospectively from May 19, 2023 and vests transfers and postings through a National Capital Civil Services Authority.

items.headline: Supreme Court stays Rahul Gandhi's conviction in 'Modi surname' defamation case
items.text: A bench of Justices B.R. Gavai, P.S. Narasimha and Sanjay Kumar stayed Rahul Gandhi's conviction, noting the trial judge gave no reasons for awarding the maximum two-year sentence that triggered disqualification under the Representation of the People Act. His Lok Sabha membership was subsequently restored.

items.headline: Rajya Sabha passes Advocates (Amendment) Bill to curb court touts
items.text: The Advocates (Amendment) Bill, 2023, introduced on August 1, was passed by the Rajya Sabha. It repeals the Legal Practitioners Act, 1879 and moves provisions on touts into the Advocates Act, 1961, allowing courts to frame lists of touts and exclude them from court premises.

items.headline: Constitution Bench begins hearing challenge to abrogation of Article 370
items.text: A five-judge Constitution Bench led by CJI DY Chandrachud began hearing the petitions challenging the 2019 abrogation of Article 370 and the bifurcation of Jammu and Kashmir. Judgment was reserved on September 5, 2023.

items.headline: Parliament passes Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill decriminalising minor offences
items.text: The Rajya Sabha passed the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2023, already passed by the Lok Sabha on July 27. It amends 42 central laws to decriminalise or rationalise minor offences, replacing several imprisonment provisions with monetary penalties.

items.headline: Parliament passes Cinematograph (Amendment) Bill, 2023 against film piracy
items.text: The Cinematograph (Amendment) Bill, 2023 was passed by Rajya Sabha on July 27 and Lok Sabha on July 31, 2023. It amends the Cinematograph Act, 1952 to add age-based certification categories and make unauthorised recording and exhibition of films an offence.
items.why: Brings piracy within the film certification law.

items.headline: Bhima Koregaon: Supreme Court grants bail to Vernon Gonsalves and Arun Ferreira
items.text: In Vernon v. State of Maharashtra (2023 LiveLaw (SC) 575; 2023 INSC 655), the Supreme Court granted bail to Vernon Gonsalves and Arun Ferreira, holding that mere possession of literature propagating violent ideology does not by itself make out a terrorist act under the UAPA.
items.why: Clarifies the prima facie test for bail under UAPA.

items.headline: Lok Sabha passes Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill
items.text: The Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2023, introduced on July 26, was passed by Lok Sabha on July 28, 2023. It amends the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957.
items.why: Paves the way for exploration licences for critical minerals.

items.headline: Lok Sabha passes National Dental Commission and Nursing Commission Bills
items.text: On July 28, 2023 Lok Sabha passed the National Dental Commission Bill, 2023, repealing the Dentists Act, 1948, and the National Nursing and Midwifery Commission Bill, 2023, repealing the Indian Nursing Council Act, 1947. Both set up new national regulators.
items.why: Replaces decades-old professional regulators.

items.headline: Lok Sabha passes Repealing and Amending Bill, 2022 scrapping obsolete laws
items.text: Lok Sabha passed the Repealing and Amending Bill, 2022. It repeals 65 obsolete laws along with a number of Appropriation Acts that are no longer needed.
items.why: Part of the clean-up of redundant central statutes.

items.headline: Lok Sabha passes Forest (Conservation) Amendment Bill, 2023
items.text: Lok Sabha passed the Forest (Conservation) Amendment Bill, 2023 on July 26, 2023. The Joint Parliamentary Committee had endorsed the Bill on July 20 with five dissent notes. The Bill exempts certain categories of land from the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980.

items.headline: Supreme Court takes suo motu cognizance of Manipur video of women paraded naked
items.text: A bench led by CJI DY Chandrachud took suo motu cognizance of the viral video from Manipur showing two women being paraded naked, calling the use of women as instruments of violence unacceptable, and asked the Centre and State to report action taken, warning the Court would act if the government did not.

items.headline: Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and S.V. Bhatti sworn in as Supreme Court judges
items.text: Justices Ujjal Bhuyan (Chief Justice, Telangana High Court) and S.V. Bhatti (Chief Justice, Kerala High Court) took oath as Supreme Court judges, raising the Court's working strength to 32. The Collegium had recommended them on July 5 and the Centre notified the appointments on July 12.

items.headline: Supreme Court holds extensions to ED Director S.K. Mishra illegal
items.text: In Dr. Jaya Thakur v. Union of India (2023 LiveLaw (SC) 518; 2023 INSC 616), the Supreme Court held the extensions granted to ED Director S.K. Mishra violated its 2021 Common Cause ruling, but allowed him to continue till July 31, 2023. It upheld the CVC and DSPE Act amendments allowing tenure extensions up to five years.

items.headline: Gujarat High Court refuses to suspend Rahul Gandhi's defamation conviction
items.text: The Gujarat High Court dismissed Rahul Gandhi's revision plea seeking suspension of his conviction in the criminal defamation case over his 'Modi surname' remark, keeping his disqualification as MP in place.

items.headline: Karnataka High Court dismisses Twitter's challenge to blocking orders with Rs 50 lakh costs
items.text: The Karnataka High Court dismissed Twitter's (now X Corp) petition challenging the Centre's blocking orders under Section 69A of the IT Act for accounts and tweets, and imposed costs of Rs 50 lakh on the company.

items.headline: CERT-In issues information security guidelines for government entities
items.text: CERT-In issued guidelines on information security practices for government entities under the Information Technology Act, 2000. They set cybersecurity compliance requirements for ministries, departments and other government bodies.

items.headline: Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, 2023 notified under Energy Conservation Act
items.text: The Ministry of Power notified the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, 2023 under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001. It sets up the framework for an Indian carbon market in which carbon credit certificates can be issued and traded.
items.why: Creates the legal basis for India's carbon market.

items.body: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
items.headline: Draft Green Credit Programme Implementation Rules released
items.text: The Environment Ministry invited comments on the draft Green Credit Programme Implementation Rules, 2023. The rules propose a mechanism for awarding tradeable green credits for voluntary environmental actions.
items.why: Final Green Credit Rules were notified in October 2023.

items.headline: Consumer Protection (Direct Selling) Rules, 2021 amended
items.text: The Ministry of Consumer Affairs notified amendments to the Consumer Protection (Direct Selling) Rules, 2021, framed under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, changing obligations on direct selling entities.

items.headline: Supreme Court holds Competition Act applies to Coal India
items.text: In Coal India Ltd v. Competition Commission of India (2023 LiveLaw (SC) 484), the Supreme Court held that Coal India, despite being a public sector undertaking governed by the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, is subject to the Competition Act, 2002.

items.headline: Law Commission invites public views on Uniform Civil Code
items.text: The 22nd Law Commission issued a public notice soliciting views from the public and recognised religious organisations on a Uniform Civil Code, with the consultation window running from June 14 to July 28, 2023.

items.headline: Supreme Court: BCI can insist that only graduates of recognised law colleges enrol as advocates
items.text: In Bar Council of India v. Rabi Sahu (2023 LiveLaw (SC) 481), the Supreme Court held that the Bar Council of India is empowered to prescribe that only those holding law degrees from colleges recognised by it can be enrolled as advocates.

items.headline: Bar Council of Delhi committee opposes BCI rules allowing foreign lawyers and law firms
items.text: A special committee of the Bar Council of Delhi issued an interim report opposing the BCI's March 2023 rules for registration of foreign lawyers and law firms, saying they would undermine the Indian legal profession, and called on the BCI to stay the rules.

items.headline: Law Commission recommends retaining sedition law with higher punishment
items.text: In Report No. 279, the 22nd Law Commission recommended retaining Section 124A IPC with amendments incorporating the Kedar Nath Singh test, raising the maximum jail term to seven years, and requiring a preliminary inquiry by an Inspector-level officer and government sanction before an FIR.
items.why: Came while sedition prosecutions stood suspended by the Supreme Court.

items.headline: Draft Aircraft Bill, 2023 released to replace Aircraft Act, 1934
items.text: The Ministry of Civil Aviation released the draft Aircraft Bill, 2023 for public feedback. It proposes to replace the Aircraft Act, 1934 with simplified provisions and wider rule-making powers for the central government.
items.why: Would overhaul the 89-year-old aviation statute.

items.body: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
items.headline: Tobacco rules amended to require anti-tobacco warnings on OTT content
items.text: The Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation) Rules, 2004 were amended. Online curated content (OTT platforms) depicting tobacco products or their use must now carry anti-tobacco health spots and warnings.
items.why: Extends COTPA content rules to streaming platforms.

items.headline: CLAT 2024 to be held on December 3, 2023
items.text: The Consortium of National Law Universities announced that CLAT 2024, for UG and PG admissions to 22 NLUs, will be held on December 3, 2023. The decision was taken at its Executive Committee and Governing Body meeting on May 20 at NLIU Bhopal.

items.headline: Justice Prashant Kumar Mishra and K.V. Viswanathan sworn in; Supreme Court at full strength of 34
items.text: Justice Prashant Kumar Mishra, Chief Justice of the Andhra Pradesh High Court, and Senior Advocate K.V. Viswanathan took oath as Supreme Court judges, administered by CJI DY Chandrachud. Viswanathan was elevated directly from the Bar.

items.headline: Centre promulgates GNCTD (Amendment) Ordinance, 2023 on Delhi services
items.text: The Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi (Amendment) Ordinance, 2023 was promulgated, taking 'services' out of the Delhi Legislative Assembly's domain and creating a National Capital Civil Services Authority to recommend transfers and postings of officers.
items.why: Effectively nullified the May 11 Constitution Bench ruling.

items.headline: Supreme Court upholds laws permitting Jallikattu, Kambala and bullock-cart races
items.text: In The Animal Welfare Board of India v. Union of India, a Constitution Bench upheld the Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Maharashtra amendments to the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 that permit Jallikattu, Kambala and bullock-cart racing, holding that the amended laws minimise cruelty to animals.

items.headline: Arjun Ram Meghwal replaces Kiren Rijiju as Union Law Minister
items.text: In a Cabinet reshuffle, Arjun Ram Meghwal was given independent charge of the Ministry of Law and Justice, replacing Kiren Rijiju, who was moved to the Ministry of Earth Sciences. Rijiju's tenure had been marked by public criticism of the collegium system.

items.headline: FEMA rules amended to bring overseas credit card spends under LRS
items.text: The Finance Ministry notified the Foreign Exchange Management (Current Account Transactions) (Amendment) Rules, 2023. They removed the exemption for international credit card spends, bringing them within the Liberalised Remittance Scheme and its tax collected at source.
items.why: Implementation was later put on hold in June 2023.

items.headline: Constitution Bench: Delhi Government, not LG, controls services except police, public order and land
items.text: In Government of NCT of Delhi v. Union of India, a five-judge Constitution Bench unanimously held that the elected Delhi Government has legislative and executive control over administrative services, excluding police, public order and land. The Lieutenant Governor is bound by the Council of Ministers' aid and advice on such matters.
items.why: Triggered the Centre's GNCTD Ordinance a week later.

items.headline: Maharashtra crisis: Governor's floor test call wrong, but Uddhav Thackeray govt cannot be restored
items.text: In Subhash Desai v. Principal Secretary, Governor of Maharashtra, a Constitution Bench held that the Governor erred in calling for a floor test and that the political party, not the legislature party, appoints the whip. It declined to restore the Thackeray government since he resigned without facing the floor test, and referred the Nabam Rebia issue to a larger bench.

items.headline: Supreme Court directs all States and UTs to register suo motu FIRs for hate speech
items.text: In the hate speech matter (Shaheen Abdulla v. Union of India), the Supreme Court extended its earlier directions to all States and Union Territories, requiring them to register FIRs suo motu against hate speech irrespective of the speaker's religion, without waiting for a complaint. Delay was to be treated as contempt.
items.why: Extends a police duty to act against hate speech nationwide.

items.headline: BCI declares AIBE XVII results
items.text: The Bar Council of India declared the results of the All India Bar Examination XVII, held on February 5, 2023 across 53 cities. About 1.71 lakh candidates had taken the exam; the final answer key was released on April 20.

items.headline: BCI passes resolution urging Supreme Court to leave same-sex marriage issue to Parliament
items.text: A joint meeting of the Bar Council of India and State Bar Councils passed a resolution asking the Supreme Court to leave the question of legal recognition of same-sex marriage to the legislative process. The resolution drew criticism from sections of the Bar and law students.

items.headline: Surat court refuses to stay Rahul Gandhi's conviction in 'Modi surname' defamation case
items.text: A Sessions Court in Surat dismissed Rahul Gandhi's application seeking suspension of his conviction in the criminal defamation case over his 'Modi surname' remark. The conviction had led to his disqualification from the Lok Sabha.

items.headline: Collegium recommends Justice S.V. Bhatti as Chief Justice of Kerala High Court
items.text: The Supreme Court Collegium recommended Justice S.V. Bhatti as Chief Justice of the Kerala High Court, succeeding Justice S. Manikumar who was due to retire on April 24, 2023. The Collegium noted his experience as a senior puisne judge in two High Courts.

items.headline: Constitution Bench begins hearing marriage equality petitions
items.text: A five-judge Constitution Bench led by CJI DY Chandrachud began hearing Supriyo v. Union of India, the batch of petitions seeking legal recognition of same-sex marriages. On day one, the Court said it would confine itself to the Special Marriage Act and not deal with personal laws for now.

items.headline: Competition (Amendment) Act, 2023 receives Presidential assent
items.text: The Competition (Amendment) Act, 2023 (No. 9 of 2023) received the President's assent on April 11, 2023. It introduces a deal-value threshold for merger notification, a settlement and commitment mechanism, and global-turnover-based penalties.
items.why: Most significant overhaul of Indian competition law since 2002.

items.headline: Centre notifies IT Rules amendments on online gaming and government fact-check unit
items.text: MeitY notified amendments to the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, providing for self-regulatory bodies to verify permissible online games and banning wagering games. The amendments also created a Fact Check Unit to flag 'fake or misleading' information about government business, which intermediaries must not host.
items.why: The fact-check unit provision was immediately challenged before the Bombay High Court.

items.headline: Supreme Court lifts telecast ban on MediaOne, faults sealed-cover procedure
items.text: In Madhyamam Broadcasting Ltd v. Union of India, the Supreme Court set aside the Centre's refusal to renew MediaOne's broadcast licence. It held that 'national security' cannot be invoked in a vacuum to deny citizens' rights and that sealed-cover proceedings violated natural justice.
items.why: Sets limits on use of national security and sealed covers to curb press freedom.

items.headline: Lok Sabha passes Competition (Amendment) Bill
items.text: The Lok Sabha passed the Competition (Amendment) Bill, 2022, which introduces a deal-value threshold for merger control, shortens timelines for approval of combinations and adds a settlement and commitment mechanism.

items.headline: Parliament passes Finance Bill, 2023 with 64 amendments
items.text: Parliament passed the Finance Bill, 2023 with 64 amendments, including changes to income tax slabs and to the tax treatment of capital gains on certain debt mutual funds.

items.headline: Draft rules propose mandatory time-of-day electricity tariffs
items.text: The Ministry of Power sought comments on the draft Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Amendment Rules, 2023. The draft would make time-of-day tariffs mandatory for consumers, including those with smart meters, under the Electricity Act, 2003.

items.headline: JPC submits report on Jan Vishwas Bill
items.text: The Joint Parliamentary Committee on the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2022 submitted its report, recommending enhanced penalties in some cases and adjudication mechanisms across the 42 laws the Bill amends.

items.headline: BCI permits foreign lawyers and law firms to practise foreign law and international arbitration in India
items.text: The Bar Council of India notified rules for registration and regulation of foreign lawyers and foreign law firms, allowing them to practise foreign law, international law and international arbitration matters in India on a reciprocal basis, while barring appearance before Indian courts.
items.why: Opens the Indian legal market to foreign firms for the first time.

items.headline: Inter-Services Organisations (Command, Control and Discipline) Bill introduced
items.text: The Inter-Services Organisations (Command, Control and Discipline) Bill, 2023 was introduced in the Lok Sabha to empower commanders of inter-services organisations to exercise disciplinary and administrative control over personnel of all three services under them.

items.headline: Forest (Conservation) Amendment Bill, 2023 introduced and sent to Joint Committee
items.text: The Forest (Conservation) Amendment Bill, 2023 was introduced in Lok Sabha and referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee. It amends the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 to exempt certain land and activities, such as eco-tourism facilities and silvicultural operations, from its restrictions.
items.why: Changes the scope of India's main forest-diversion law.

items.headline: Joint Committee report on Multi-State Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Bill tabled
items.text: The Joint Parliamentary Committee examining the Multi-State Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Bill, 2022 tabled its report. It broadly endorsed the proposed amendments to the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 2002.

items.headline: Surrogacy Rules amended to require both gametes from intending couple
items.text: The Centre amended the Surrogacy (Regulation) Rules, 2022 to require that both male and female gametes come from the intending couple, effectively barring donor gametes in gestational surrogacy.
items.why: Later challenged before the Supreme Court.

items.headline: Crypto/virtual digital asset businesses brought under PMLA
items.text: The Finance Ministry notified that entities dealing in virtual digital assets, including exchanges and custodians, are 'reporting entities' under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, requiring KYC and record-keeping obligations.

items.headline: Term of 22nd Law Commission extended until August 31, 2024
items.text: The Union Cabinet approved extending the tenure of the 22nd Law Commission of India, whose Chairperson and members had been appointed in November 2022, until August 31, 2024.

items.headline: Cabinet approves ratifying amendments to Chicago Convention on civil aviation
items.text: The Union Cabinet approved ratification of three amending protocols to the Convention on International Civil Aviation (Chicago Convention), 1944. The amendments raise the strength of the ICAO Council from 36 to 40 members and enlarge the Air Navigation Commission.

items.body: Securities and Exchange Board of India
items.headline: SEBI proposes corporate governance changes to LODR Regulations
items.text: SEBI released a consultation paper proposing amendments to the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. Proposals covered disclosure of shareholder agreements, ending permanent board seats and shareholder approval for sale of assets.
items.why: Affects governance obligations of listed companies.

items.body: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
items.headline: Draft rules would make coal power plants burn crop residue pellets
items.text: The Environment Ministry released the draft Agro Residue Utilisation by Thermal Power Plants Rules, 2023. Coal-based thermal power plants would have to use at least 5% pellets made from crop residue, blended with coal, every year.
items.why: Legal mandate aimed at reducing stubble burning.

items.headline: Justices Rajesh Bindal and Aravind Kumar sworn in; Supreme Court at full strength of 34
items.text: Justices Rajesh Bindal and Aravind Kumar, former Chief Justices of the Allahabad and Gujarat High Courts, took oath as Supreme Court judges on February 13, 2023, taking the Court to its full sanctioned strength of 34 judges.

items.headline: First part of Budget Session 2023 ends; Jan Vishwas and Competition Bills pending
items.text: The first part of the Budget Session concluded on February 13, 2023. Bills listed for consideration included the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2022, the Competition (Amendment) Bill, 2022 and the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Bill, 2022.

items.headline: Draft amendments to Offshore Areas Mineral Act, 2002 released
items.text: The Ministry of Mines released draft amendments to the Offshore Areas Mineral (Development and Regulation) Act, 2002. They propose composite exploration-cum-production licences, raise the production lease period from 30 to 50 years and shrink the standard offshore mineral block size.
items.why: Precursor to the Offshore Areas Mineral Amendment Bill, 2023.

items.headline: Five new judges sworn in to the Supreme Court
items.text: Justices Pankaj Mithal, Sanjay Karol, P.V. Sanjay Kumar, Ahsanuddin Amanullah and Manoj Misra took oath as Supreme Court judges on February 6, 2023, following the Collegium's December 2022 recommendation.

items.headline: AIBE-XVII: BCI allows candidates to carry bare Acts ahead of February 5 exam
items.text: The Bar Council of India allowed candidates appearing in the All India Bar Examination XVII on February 5, 2023 to carry downloaded or printed copies of bare Acts with minimal notes. The exam was eventually taken by over 1.7 lakh candidates across 53 cities.

items.headline: Inter-ministerial committee set up on human rights treaty obligations
items.text: The Centre constituted an inter-ministerial committee on human rights. It is tasked with implementing India's obligations under human rights treaties and following up on recommendations from the UN Universal Periodic Review.

items.headline: Budget Session 2023 begins with President's address to joint sitting
items.text: Parliament's Budget Session 2023 began on January 31, 2023 with the President addressing a joint sitting of both Houses. The session was scheduled for 27 sittings in two parts: January 31 to February 13 and March 13 to April 6, 2023.
items.why: Sets the legislative calendar for Budget 2023-24 and pending Bills.

items.headline: TRAI consults on converging regulation of broadcasting and telecom carriage
items.text: TRAI released a consultation paper on enabling convergence in the carriage of broadcasting and telecommunication services. It flagged that telecom, broadcasting and IT services are governed by different Acts and ministries, and sought views on a unified framework.
items.why: Relevant to any future unified communications law.

items.headline: In a first, SC Collegium publishes Centre's objections and its reasons for reiterating names including Saurabh Kirpal
items.text: The Supreme Court Collegium made public the Centre's objections, based on IB and RAW inputs, to candidates for High Court judgeship, including Saurabh Kirpal (sexual orientation, foreign partner), Somasekhar Sundaresan and R. John Sathyan (social media posts), and recorded its reasons for rejecting them and reiterating the names.
items.why: Unprecedented transparency in the appointments standoff.

items.headline: Draft amendments to Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code released for consultation
items.text: The Ministry of Corporate Affairs released draft amendments to the IBC, 2016 proposing wider eligibility for pre-packaged insolvency, lowering the creditor approval threshold for pre-packs from 66% to 51%, and provisions for real estate insolvency cases.

items.headline: Draft IT Rules amendment on PIB fact-check and online gaming released
items.text: MeitY released draft amendments to the IT Rules, 2021 requiring intermediaries not to publish content flagged as false or fake by the PIB fact-check unit or other authorised agencies, and proposing a framework for online gaming.
items.why: Drew criticism from media bodies over government fact-checking powers.

items.headline: Law Minister defends letter to CJI seeking government nominees in judge-selection panel
items.text: Law Minister Kiren Rijiju defended his letter to the CJI proposing a search-cum-evaluation committee including government representatives to prepare panels of candidates for judicial appointment, saying it followed the NJAC judgment's direction to revise the Memorandum of Procedure and did not seek a seat on the Collegium.

items.headline: RBI issues directions on acquiring and holding shares or voting rights in banks
items.text: The RBI issued the RBI (Acquisition and Holding of Shares or Voting Rights in Banking Companies) Directions, 2023. They lay down requirements for acquiring a major shareholding in a banking company and set shareholding limits for different categories of investors.
items.why: Governs who can own significant stakes in Indian banks.

items.body: Securities and Exchange Board of India
items.headline: SEBI consults on allowing private equity funds to sponsor mutual funds
items.text: SEBI released a consultation paper reviewing the regulatory framework for mutual fund sponsors. Among other things, it proposed alternative eligibility criteria under which private equity funds could act as sponsors of mutual funds.
items.why: Could widen who may set up mutual funds under SEBI regulations.

items.headline: No additional restrictions on free speech of ministers beyond Article 19(2): SC (Kaushal Kishor v. State of UP)
items.text: A Constitution Bench held that grounds in Article 19(2) are exhaustive and no additional restrictions can be imposed on the free speech of public functionaries, and that a minister's statement cannot be vicariously attributed to the government. Justice Nagarathna partly dissented.

items.headline: Supreme Court upholds 2016 demonetisation by 4:1 (Vivek Narayan Sharma v. Union of India)
items.text: A five-judge Constitution Bench upheld the November 2016 demonetisation of Rs 500 and Rs 1000 notes, holding that the decision-making process under Section 26(2) of the RBI Act was not flawed and that hardship to citizens did not render it invalid. Justice B.V. Nagarathna dissented, holding the measure should have been done through legislation.
